launch-la-new-orleans-new-orleans-city-p.summary: A 1,300-acre free public landscape of live oaks, lagoons, playgrounds, trails, sculpture, museums, gardens, family attractions, sports, boating, food, festivals, and forest habitat.
launch-la-new-orleans-new-orleans-city-p.hours: Park grounds are open sunrise to sunset every day; museums, gardens, amusement areas, food, rentals, sports facilities, and events keep separate schedules.
launch-la-new-orleans-new-orleans-city-p.parking: Free parking is distributed across the enormous park. Route to the exact attraction instead of 1 Palm Drive; NOMA, Children's Museum, Carousel Gardens, Couturie Forest, Big Lake, and sports areas use different lots.
launch-la-new-orleans-new-orleans-city-p.arrival: Choose the south cultural core, family-attraction core, Big Lake, Couturie Forest, festival grounds, or athletic areas before driving. Distances are too large to treat every attraction as one stop.
launch-la-new-orleans-new-orleans-city-p.restrooms: Public restrooms are mapped at selected visitor nodes and inside operating attractions; do not assume every playground, trail, or lagoon edge has facilities.
launch-la-new-orleans-new-orleans-city-p.cost: Grounds, four playgrounds, trails, disc golf, Big Lake, Couturie Forest, and the Besthoff Sculpture Garden are free. Museums, gardens, rides, mini golf, rentals, food, golf, and events may charge.
launch-la-new-orleans-new-orleans-city-p.accessibility: Major attractions have accessible parking and routes, but historic paths, forest trails, bridges, roots, lawns, and long distances vary. Select the nearest destination entrance.
launch-la-new-orleans-new-orleans-city-p.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed in ordinary outdoor areas under posted rules; attractions, playgrounds, gardens, food areas, events, and athletic facilities may restrict them.
launch-la-new-orleans-new-orleans-city-p.family: This is New Orleans' broadest family park, but a successful visit needs a short destination list. Free playgrounds and sculpture pair well; ticketed rides, Storyland, and the Children's Museum require schedule checks.
launch-la-new-orleans-new-orleans-city-p.transit: Streetcar, bus, bike, Lafitte Greenway, rideshare, and driving reach different park edges. The Canal streetcar terminus is useful for the southern core but not every northern destination.
launch-la-new-orleans-new-orleans-city-p.need: The park is free to enter but not everything inside is free or open on the same schedule. Heat, thunderstorms, festivals, construction, flooding, and seasonal attraction hours can change the best route.

launch-la-new-orleans-audubon-park.summary: A historic Uptown park stretching from St. Charles Avenue to the Mississippi River, with a popular paved loop, lagoon, oaks, playgrounds, zoo, golf, shelters, rookery, and The Fly riverfront.
launch-la-new-orleans-audubon-park.hours: Public outdoor areas generally open daily around 5:00 a.m. and close at 10:00 p.m.; Audubon Zoo, golf, shelters, and events use separate hours.
launch-la-new-orleans-audubon-park.parking: Free curb and park-edge parking is dispersed along Magazine Street, St. Charles Avenue, Walnut Street, and Riverview. Zoo demand and events can fill the closest spaces.
launch-la-new-orleans-audubon-park.arrival: Use St. Charles for the classic park and loop, Magazine Street for zoo and playground access, or Riverview Drive for The Fly. The riverfront is separated from the main lawn by zoo and rail infrastructure.
launch-la-new-orleans-audubon-park.restrooms: Restrooms are concentrated near playgrounds, shelters, zoo, golf, and Riverview facilities and may follow facility hours.
launch-la-new-orleans-audubon-park.cost: Park paths, lawns, playgrounds, lagoon, labyrinth, rookery viewing, and The Fly are free. Zoo, golf, food, rentals, permits, and events cost separately.
launch-la-new-orleans-audubon-park.accessibility: The paved loop and major developed areas are generally accessible; curb transitions, older paths, grass, crowding, and the Riverview approach vary.
launch-la-new-orleans-audubon-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed in ordinary park and Riverview areas; keep pets out of playgrounds, zoo, golf course, bird rookery habitat, and posted restricted spaces.
launch-la-new-orleans-audubon-park.family: The loop, lagoon, playgrounds, zoo, picnics, and river watching provide strong options. Choose either the main park or The Fly first to avoid a long, confusing transfer.
launch-la-new-orleans-audubon-park.transit: St. Charles streetcar and buses serve the Uptown side; biking and rideshare work well. Reaching The Fly still requires crossing to the river side.
launch-la-new-orleans-audubon-park.need: The paved loop is shared by runners, walkers, strollers, and cyclists. The lagoon is not for swimming, Ochsner Island is protected bird habitat, and riverfront activity can be hot and exposed.

launch-la-new-orleans-crescent-park.address: 2300 North Peters Street, New Orleans, LA 70117
launch-la-new-orleans-crescent-park.summary: A 1.4-mile linear Mississippi River park through Marigny and Bywater with skyline views, wharves, lawns, pavilions, public art, a dog run, and dramatic bridge entrances.
launch-la-new-orleans-crescent-park.hours: Crescent Park is generally open daily 6:00 a.m.-7:30 p.m.; gates, events, maintenance, storms, and river conditions may alter access, so confirm posted hours.
launch-la-new-orleans-crescent-park.parking: There is no single central lot. Use legal neighborhood parking near Elysian Fields, Piety, Mazant, or Bartholomew access and never block driveways or signed residential zones.
launch-la-new-orleans-crescent-park.arrival: Select an entrance before travel. The Rusty Rainbow at Piety requires a large stair-and-ramp climb; Mazant and Bartholomew offer different approaches along the long riverfront.
launch-la-new-orleans-crescent-park.restrooms: Restroom availability is limited and can be event-dependent. Do not begin a long linear walk assuming facilities will be open at the far end.
launch-la-new-orleans-crescent-park.cost: Park entry, paths, lawns, overlooks, pavilions, and dog run are free. Parking, nearby food, permits, and events may cost.
launch-la-new-orleans-crescent-park.accessibility: Long paved paths are generally accessible, but the Piety bridge has substantial elevation and distance. Choose a lower-grade access and plan the return trip.
launch-la-new-orleans-crescent-park.dogs: Dogs must be leashed outside the designated dog run. Bring water and waste bags, and keep pets away from rail operations and river edges.
launch-la-new-orleans-crescent-park.family: Open lawns, ship watching, swings, and broad paths can work well, but there is little conventional playground equipment and the river/rail setting requires close supervision.
launch-la-new-orleans-crescent-park.transit: Walking and biking from the French Quarter, Marigny, and Bywater are practical; transit and rideshare should target the exact entrance rather than the park name.
launch-la-new-orleans-crescent-park.need: This is a linear trip, not a loop. Heat, limited shade, freight activity, river weather, locked gates, and the distance back to your starting point are the main planning issues.

launch-la-new-orleans-louis-armstrong-pa.address: 701 North Rampart Street, New Orleans, LA 70116
launch-la-new-orleans-louis-armstrong-pa.summary: A 31-acre Tremé cultural landscape across from the French Quarter containing Congo Square, lagoons, bridges, sculpture, historic structures, theaters, lawns, and foundational Black music history.
launch-la-new-orleans-louis-armstrong-pa.hours: Open daily 8:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m. in winter and 8:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. during daylight saving time; events may change gates and access.
launch-la-new-orleans-louis-armstrong-pa.parking: Use paid French Quarter or Tremé street parking and garages, transit, biking, walking, or rideshare. There is no large free visitor lot dedicated to the park.
launch-la-new-orleans-louis-armstrong-pa.arrival: The ceremonial arch on North Rampart is the clearest general entrance; Congo Square sits toward St. Peter Street and event venues have separate controlled entries.
launch-la-new-orleans-louis-armstrong-pa.restrooms: Do not rely on always-open public restrooms inside the landscape. Event venues and nearby visitor businesses provide facilities only during their operating hours.
launch-la-new-orleans-louis-armstrong-pa.cost: Ordinary park and Congo Square access are free. Performances, parking, permits, tours, food, and special events may charge.
launch-la-new-orleans-louis-armstrong-pa.accessibility: Major paths and entrances are paved, but bridges, older surfaces, temporary event barriers, and closed buildings can affect routes.
launch-la-new-orleans-louis-armstrong-pa.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary outdoor areas under city rules; events, theaters, cultural programs, and posted areas may restrict pets.
launch-la-new-orleans-louis-armstrong-pa.family: The open landscape, bridges, sculpture, music history, and Congo Square can support a short family visit, but there is no playground and water edges need supervision.
launch-la-new-orleans-louis-armstrong-pa.transit: Rampart streetcar service, buses, walking, biking, and rideshare make this one of the easiest car-free parks to reach from the French Quarter.
launch-la-new-orleans-louis-armstrong-pa.need: Congo Square is a living cultural site, not simply an event lawn. Respect ceremonies and performances; verify gates and events, and do not assume the Municipal Auditorium or Perseverance Hall is open.

launch-la-new-orleans-lafitte-greenway.summary: A roughly 2.6-mile walking and biking corridor linking the edge of the French Quarter with Tremé, Lafitte, Mid-City, and Bayou St. John through parks, recreation, art, gardens, and stormwater landscapes.
launch-la-new-orleans-lafitte-greenway.hours: The public greenway is intended for daily transportation and recreation; developed facilities, playgrounds, courts, lighting, programs, and adjacent businesses use separate schedules.
launch-la-new-orleans-lafitte-greenway.parking: Use legal neighborhood parking only if necessary. The greenway works best as a bike, walk, transit, or point-to-point route; do not leave valuables visible in vehicles.
launch-la-new-orleans-lafitte-greenway.arrival: Choose a trailhead or cross street. North Claiborne, Broad, Norman C. Francis, Bayou St. John, and the Mid-City end lead to different amenities.
launch-la-new-orleans-lafitte-greenway.restrooms: Reliable always-open public restrooms are limited along the corridor. Recreation facilities and businesses have independent access and hours.
launch-la-new-orleans-lafitte-greenway.cost: The trail, public landscapes, art, basketball, and ordinary recreation are free. Programs, rentals, food, and events may charge.
launch-la-new-orleans-lafitte-greenway.accessibility: The paved shared-use path is generally accessible, but street crossings, construction, drainage, crowds, and temporary detours require attention.
launch-la-new-orleans-lafitte-greenway.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed; keep them short at crossings and around bikes, runners, playgrounds, courts, gardens, and food areas.
launch-la-new-orleans-lafitte-greenway.family: Short sections near playgrounds, FitLot, art, and Bayou St. John suit families. The full corridor includes busy street crossings and fast bicycle traffic.
launch-la-new-orleans-lafitte-greenway.transit: The greenway is itself a car-free connector and intersects bus, streetcar, bikeshare, neighborhood bicycle, and walking routes.
launch-la-new-orleans-lafitte-greenway.need: This is a transportation corridor as well as a park. Keep right, signal passing, supervise children at every street crossing, and check current construction or extension detours.

launch-la-new-orleans-goldring-woldenber.summary: A newly continuous 2.25-mile downtown riverfront system connecting Spanish Plaza toward Crescent Park, with promenades, lawns, public art, a marsh-themed playground, cooling misters, and the covered NOLA Front Porch.
launch-la-new-orleans-goldring-woldenber.hours: Open Sunday-Thursday 6:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. and Friday-Saturday 6:00 a.m.-midnight; Aquarium, ferry, events, food, and individual facilities keep separate schedules.
launch-la-new-orleans-goldring-woldenber.parking: Use paid downtown garages, metered spaces, transit, ferry, walking, biking, or rideshare. The park does not provide one large free visitor lot.
launch-la-new-orleans-goldring-woldenber.arrival: Choose Canal Street/Spanish Plaza for the Aquarium and ferry, or St. Philip Street for the 2026 Governor Nicholls expansion, playground, and NOLA Front Porch.
launch-la-new-orleans-goldring-woldenber.restrooms: Restroom access varies across the long riverfront and may depend on operating attractions or event facilities. Plan a known stop before walking the full corridor.
launch-la-new-orleans-goldring-woldenber.cost: Public park access, river views, paths, lawns, playground, misters, and Front Porch are free. Aquarium, parking, ferry fares, food, and events cost separately.
launch-la-new-orleans-goldring-woldenber.accessibility: The renewed riverfront emphasizes continuous paved access, but long distances, transitions between phases, event barriers, and historic edges still require route planning.
launch-la-new-orleans-goldring-woldenber.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary public outdoor areas; playgrounds, Aquarium spaces, events, food areas, and ferry operations have separate restrictions.
launch-la-new-orleans-goldring-woldenber.family: The new marsh playground, shaded seating, cooling misters, ships, Aquarium plaza, and broad promenade create a strong downtown family destination.
launch-la-new-orleans-goldring-woldenber.transit: Canal streetcar, buses, ferry, biking, walking, and rideshare reach the riverfront. Plan different start and finish points for the full 2.25-mile route.
launch-la-new-orleans-goldring-woldenber.need: The riverfront changed substantially in April 2026. Use St. Philip Street for the new playground phase, watch children beside the working river, and check storms, heat, events, and ferry conditions.

launch-la-new-orleans-jackson-square.summary: New Orleans' landmark 2.5-acre formal square facing St. Louis Cathedral, framed by museums and historic buildings and surrounded by artists, performers, river overlooks, and French Quarter activity.
launch-la-new-orleans-jackson-square.hours: Open daily 8:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m. in winter and 8:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. during daylight saving time; ceremonies, maintenance, filming, and permitted events may alter access.
launch-la-new-orleans-jackson-square.parking: Do not expect parking at the square. Walk, use transit or rideshare, or choose a paid French Quarter garage; metered spaces are scarce and tightly regulated.
launch-la-new-orleans-jackson-square.arrival: The enclosed garden has gates on each side. Decatur Street connects toward the river; Chartres Street faces the cathedral, Cabildo, and Presbytère.
launch-la-new-orleans-jackson-square.restrooms: There are no dependable always-open public restrooms inside the small formal garden. Nearby museums, visitor facilities, and businesses have their own rules and hours.
launch-la-new-orleans-jackson-square.cost: Entering the square and viewing the exterior landscape are free. Museums, tours, parking, food, performers, portraits, and events cost separately.
launch-la-new-orleans-jackson-square.accessibility: The central paths and perimeter are compact, but crowds, curbs, uneven historic paving, performers, and temporary closures can complicate movement.
launch-la-new-orleans-jackson-square.dogs: Leashed dogs are subject to posted park and French Quarter rules; museums, cathedral, crowds, performers, and events may not accommodate pets.
launch-la-new-orleans-jackson-square.family: The compact garden, cathedral view, statue, artists, carriages, and river overlook are visually engaging, but there is no playground and crowds require close supervision.
launch-la-new-orleans-jackson-square.transit: Streetcars, buses, ferry connections, walking, biking, and rideshare serve the French Quarter; driving directly to the square is usually the least efficient choice.
launch-la-new-orleans-jackson-square.need: Jackson Square is only the gated garden, while many experiences associated with it sit outside the fence. Gates close earlier than the surrounding French Quarter, and formal photography or events require permits.

launch-la-new-orleans-bayou-sauvage-urba.address: 17160 Chef Menteur Highway, New Orleans, LA 70129
launch-la-new-orleans-bayou-sauvage-urba.summary: A 27,190-acre urban national wildlife refuge of marshes, lagoons, forests, bayous, levees, fishing, paddling, birding, photography, and self-guided nature access in eastern New Orleans.
launch-la-new-orleans-bayou-sauvage-urba.hours: Open daily during daylight hours only and closed at night. Seasonal hunting restrictions delay entry outside the Hurricane Protection Levee until noon during teal season and November 1-January 31.
launch-la-new-orleans-bayou-sauvage-urba.parking: Use designated parking only at the selected trail, launch, or access point. Do not rely on the general refuge address to reach every public-use area.
launch-la-new-orleans-bayou-sauvage-urba.arrival: Choose Ridge Trail, Highway 11 launch, Irish Bayou, Joe Madere Marsh, or another official access before driving; mobile service and navigation can be unreliable.
launch-la-new-orleans-bayou-sauvage-urba.restrooms: Ridge Trail normally has restrooms and a picnic pavilion, but the Ridge Trail and boardwalk have been closed for reconstruction since March 2, 2026. Other remote access points may have no facilities.
launch-la-new-orleans-bayou-sauvage-urba.cost: General wildlife observation and approved public access are free. Louisiana licenses, permits, equipment, tours, and some consumptive uses may require fees or documentation.
launch-la-new-orleans-bayou-sauvage-urba.accessibility: The Ridge Trail boardwalk was the primary accessible developed route but is closed for reconstruction. Levees, launches, marsh edges, and remote terrain vary greatly.
launch-la-new-orleans-bayou-sauvage-urba.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed under refuge rules except during authorized hunting use; wildlife, alligators, heat, water, and rough access create serious pet risks.
launch-la-new-orleans-bayou-sauvage-urba.family: Wildlife viewing and short developed routes can be memorable, but this is remote habitat, not a playground. Bring water, sun and insect protection, and maintain direct child supervision.
launch-la-new-orleans-bayou-sauvage-urba.transit: A private vehicle is the practical way to reach most public access points. Confirm the exact route and tell someone your plan before entering remote areas.
launch-la-new-orleans-bayou-sauvage-urba.need: The Ridge Trail and Boardwalk remain closed for reconstruction as of this review. Never feed wildlife, expect alligators and insects, carry no expectation of shade or services, and obey seasonal closures and gate signs.
